design: H-1 concatenated dual signature: hybrid_sig = sig_classical || sig_pq, hybrid_pk = pk_classical || pk_pq. Verification accepts only when BOTH halves verify (AND policy). No framing beyond a versioned envelope header (see docs/HYBRID_DESIGN.md).
note: Combined sizes are pure arithmetic from data/algorithm_params.json (classical bytes + post-quantum bytes, no framing). The ratio is combined_signature_bytes / 64 (Ed25519-only signature). Framing overhead is the envelope header only (algorithm identifiers + version, tens of bytes) and is excluded here; it is [SIMULATED] in docs/HYBRID_DESIGN.md. Throughput figures are NOT in this file: they come from outputs/hybrid_bench.log (measured) and are checked, not copied, by scripts/hybrid_model.py.
recommended_reason: Smallest combined signature among the category-2-or-better hybrids (2,484 bytes, 38.8x an Ed25519 signature), fastest post-quantum signing and verification of the measured set (see outputs/benchmark-pq.log), and category 2 security, which matches the classical baseline it replaces (Ed25519 ~128-bit). SLH-DSA-128f is the conservative alternative when a non-lattice assumption is required: its public key is 32 bytes, but its signature is 17,088 bytes (268x Ed25519) and its signing is far slower. ML-DSA-65/87 buy a higher NIST category at 1.4x-1.9x the ML-DSA-44 signature size; the migration plan stages them as an optional later step, not the first one.
